title: A Forced Reckoning in the Restaurant Industry

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·朗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于热爱设计及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在我还在夜店打碟的黑胶唱片时代，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每天晚上都要带着300件最珍贵的宝贝去上班，把DJ台变成了一个充满50年历史精美文物的流动快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听奥德修斯·皮盖出品的《重构者》吧。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Sabrina Tavernisi and this is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的萨布丽娜·塔弗尼西，这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: When the Me Too movement swept through the country, exposing abuses at the highest levels of power, the restaurant industry was a chief offender.
sentences.zh: 当“我也是”（Me Too）运动席卷全国，揭露最高权力层面的滥权行为时，餐饮业成了主要的违规者之一。

sentences.en: But the food world's main kingmaker, the James Beard Foundation, only recently began to reckon with that.
sentences.zh: 但餐饮界的主要造王者——詹姆斯·比尔德基金会，直到最近才开始正视这个问题。

sentences.en: Today, food writer Brett Anderson explains how those attempts to hold the industry to account prompted an entirely new firestorm.
sentences.zh: 今天，美食作家布雷特·安德森将解释这些要求行业负责的尝试，是如何引发了一场全新的风暴的。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, June 13th.
sentences.zh: 今天是6月13日，星期二。

sentences.en: So Brett, last week, the James Beard Awards were handed out.
sentences.zh: 布雷特，上周詹姆斯·比尔德奖刚刚颁发。

sentences.en: And I know the words James Beard, and I know they have something to do with food, but that's about the extent of it.
sentences.zh: 我知道“詹姆斯·比尔德”这个名字，也知道它和食物有关，但也就仅此而已了。

sentences.en: So before we get into the changes at the awards, let's start with the basics.
sentences.zh: 所以在我们讨论奖项的变革之前，先从基础知识开始吧。

sentences.en: What exactly are the James Beard Awards?
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯·比尔德奖到底是什么？

sentences.en: Well, the James Beard Awards are commonly likened to the Oscars of the food world, and I think that's a pretty apt description.
sentences.zh: 嗯，詹姆斯·比尔德奖通常被比作餐饮界的奥斯卡，我觉得这个描述非常贴切。

sentences.en: When you win a James Beard Award, you become basically forever known professionally as a beard winner.
sentences.zh: 当你赢得詹姆斯·比尔德奖后，你在职业生涯中基本上就永远被称为“比尔德奖得主”了。

sentences.en: It's something that attaches to your name that anyone in the food industry knows is recognition of some sort of accomplishment.
sentences.zh: 这是一个附加在你名字上的头衔，餐饮界的任何人都知道这是对某种成就的认可。

sentences.en: It's something that can lead to restaurant opening opportunities.
sentences.zh: 它能带来开设餐厅的机会。

sentences.en: It can lead to partnerships with hotels and casinos.
sentences.zh: 它能带来与酒店和赌场的合作。

sentences.en: It can lead to book contracts.
sentences.zh: 它能带来图书出版合同。

sentences.en: So it can transform your life.
sentences.zh: 所以它能改变你的人生。

sentences.en: It can transform your career.
sentences.zh: 它能改变你的职业生涯。

sentences.en: Okay, so these awards are a big deal.
sentences.zh: 好吧，看来这些奖项确实意义重大。

sentences.en: Who votes on them?
sentences.zh: 谁来投票呢？

sentences.en: Like, what's the system?
sentences.zh: 投票系统是怎么运作的？

sentences.en: Well, since the awards have been established, the voting body has always included food journalists, and I myself was a voter for many years.
sentences.zh: 嗯，自奖项设立以来，投票团一直包括美食记者，我自己也曾担任过多年的评委。

sentences.en: And also for a long time included past winners.
sentences.zh: 而且很长一段时间里，投票团也包括往届获奖者。

sentences.en: If you won a Beard Award, it meant you could vote on future Beard Awards.
sentences.zh: 如果你赢得了比尔德奖，就意味着你有权对未来的比尔德奖进行投票。

sentences.en: It was sort of part of the perk of winning it.
sentences.zh: 这算是获奖福利的一部分。

sentences.en: That changed in recent years, and the last two awards seasons, 2022 and the one that just completed, have involved a different voting process than they've had in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 近年来情况发生了变化，最近两个颁奖季，即2022年和刚刚结束的这一季，其投票流程与以往不同。

sentences.en: And what was different about this time?
sentences.zh: 这次有什么不同？

sentences.en: Well, historically, the Beard Awards have been meant to recognize culinary excellence, period.
sentences.zh: 从历史上看，比尔德奖旨在表彰卓越的烹饪成就，仅此而已。

sentences.en: And in recent years, the foundation, the James Beard Foundation, which is the nonprofit in New York that administers the awards,
sentences.zh: 近年来，位于纽约、负责管理该奖项的非营利组织——詹姆斯·比尔德基金会，

sentences.en: has created new criteria that is beyond culinary excellence and recognizes personal behavior as well.
sentences.zh: 制定了超越烹饪卓越性的新标准，也将个人行为纳入了考量范围。

sentences.en: Personal behavior.
sentences.zh: 个人行为。

sentences.en: Okay, so not just cooking and chefery, but actual behavior, like how the chefs themselves act.
sentences.zh: 好吧，所以不仅是烹饪和厨艺，还包括实际的行为，比如厨师们自己的表现。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think the James Beard Foundation is trying to address misbehavior and abuse in the industry that it's in, just like a lot of other entities are throughout our culture.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为詹姆斯·比尔德基金会正试图解决其所在行业内的不当行为和虐待现象，就像我们文化中的许多其他实体一样。

sentences.en: And as it happens in the restaurant industry, that's a really big job.
sentences.zh: 而在餐饮业，这确实是一项艰巨的任务。

sentences.en: There isn't a regulatory body overseeing any of that.
sentences.zh: 目前没有任何监管机构来监督这些。

sentences.en: How do you even begin to do that?
sentences.zh: 你该如何着手处理呢？

sentences.en: Maybe let's start with this James Beard Foundation.
sentences.zh: 也许我们先从这个詹姆斯·比尔德基金会说起。

sentences.en: What is it, and why is it trying to police the food world?
sentences.zh: 它是什么？为什么它要试图监管餐饮界？

sentences.en: So, James Beard was a famous cookbook author and sort of a food personality back before there was such a thing.
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯·比尔德是著名的食谱作者，也是在那个概念尚未普及之前的某种美食名人。

sentences.en: He's known as the Dean of American Cookery.
sentences.zh: 他被称为“美国烹饪界的院长”。

sentences.en: And in the 50s and in the 60s, he was influential in sort of educating Americans about their own cuisine.
sentences.zh: 在50和60年代，他在教育美国人了解本国饮食文化方面颇具影响力。

sentences.en: At a time when people thought of culinary excellence as being sort of the exclusive province of sort of French and Italians,
sentences.zh: 在那个人们认为烹饪卓越是法国和意大利人专属领域的时代，

sentences.en: he celebrated the food of Americans and the food of regional America.
sentences.zh: 他赞美了美国人的食物和美国区域性的美食。

sentences.en: And he had a lot of influence on people who his contemporaries, including Julia Child, who considered him something of a mentor and someone she really looked up to.
sentences.zh: 他对同时代的人产生了很大影响，包括朱莉娅·柴尔德，她将他视为导师，非常敬重他。

sentences.en: And after he died, those people got together and they bought his small townhouse in Greenwich Village.
sentences.zh: 他去世后，这些人聚在一起，买下了他在格林威治村的小联排别墅。

sentences.en: And in 1986, they started the James Beard Foundation in that townhouse.
sentences.zh: 1986年，他们在那个联排别墅里成立了詹姆斯·比尔德基金会。

sentences.en: And the mission at the time was to create a center for culinary arts.
sentences.zh: 当时的使命是创建一个烹饪艺术中心。

sentences.en: And it was a very, I think, small enterprise that was, you know, reflected by the smallness of the townhouse, if you've ever been there.
sentences.zh: 我认为那是一个非常小的企业，如果你去过那里，就会发现它反映了那座联排别墅的狭小。

sentences.en: Huh.
sentences.zh: 哦。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So, small group of foodies, together at this little townhouse, how does that end up becoming this giant thing that's a cane maker in the food world?
sentences.zh: 那么，一群美食家聚在这个小联排别墅里，它是如何最终变成餐饮界那个巨大的造王者的呢？

sentences.en: Well, two things happened.
sentences.zh: 嗯，发生了两件事。

sentences.en: In 1991, the Beard Foundation creates the James Beard Awards, the thing that we know today as the Oscars of the food world.
sentences.zh: 1991年，比尔德基金会创立了詹姆斯·比尔德奖，也就是我们今天所知的餐饮界奥斯卡。

sentences.en: And that turned out to be a really good timing, because right around the same time...
sentences.zh: 事实证明时机非常好，因为就在同一时间……

sentences.en: Next on Food Network, you get the creation of the Food Network.
sentences.zh: 接下来是美食频道，你迎来了美食频道的诞生。

sentences.en: The Food Network.
sentences.zh: 美食频道。

sentences.en: But today, we're going to be making some breakfast food.
sentences.zh: 但今天，我们要制作一些早餐食品。

sentences.en: You see how thin I'm slicing this?
sentences.zh: 看到我切得有多薄了吗？

sentences.en: And notice my angle.
sentences.zh: 注意我的角度。

sentences.en: I'm going not just down.
sentences.zh: 我不只是向下切。

sentences.en: I'm going across...
sentences.zh: 我横着切……

sentences.en: It started out doing shows that were really similar to what you would see on public television.
sentences.zh: 它起初制作的节目与你在公共电视上看到的非常相似。

sentences.en: It was instructional.
sentences.zh: 它是教学性质的。

sentences.en: And we're talking about the Italian cooking and our love for it.
sentences.zh: 我们正在谈论意大利烹饪以及我们对它的热爱。

sentences.en: And then it started to change.
sentences.zh: 然后它开始改变了。

sentences.en: It started to be less about cooking instruction and more about the chefs themselves.
sentences.zh: 它不再仅仅关注烹饪教学，而是更多地关注厨师本人。

sentences.en: How do you like your anchovies?
sentences.zh: 你喜欢怎么吃凤尾鱼？

sentences.en: You want to do it cross?
sentences.zh: 你想交叉着放吗？

sentences.en: Good.
sentences.zh: 很好。

sentences.en: You start to have real personalities, like Emeril Lagasse.
sentences.zh: 你开始看到真正的个性人物，比如埃梅里尔·拉加斯。

sentences.en: Oh, can you imagine being stuffed with anchovy like this?
sentences.zh: 哦，你能想象被这样塞进凤尾鱼吗？

sentences.en: Stuffed right in there like that.
sentences.zh: 就这样塞进去。

sentences.en: And stuffed!
sentences.zh: 塞满了！

sentences.en: Who had just a few restaurants in New Orleans and became known all over the country...
sentences.zh: 他当时在新奥尔良只有几家餐厅，却在全国范围内出名了……

sentences.en: Bam!
sentences.zh: 砰！

sentences.en: Bam!
sentences.zh: 砰！

sentences.en: ...for yelling bam on his show.
sentences.zh: ……因为他在节目里大喊“砰”。

sentences.en: And you just kind of bam, bam, bam, bam, bam, bam, bam!
sentences.zh: 你就这样砰、砰、砰、砰、砰、砰、砰！

sentences.en: Bobby Flay.
sentences.zh: 鲍比·弗雷。

sentences.en: All these other people.
sentences.zh: 还有所有其他人。

sentences.en: My name is Bobby Flay.
sentences.zh: 我叫鲍比·弗雷。

sentences.en: My mission?
sentences.zh: 我的使命？

sentences.en: To find the best of the beSt.
sentences.zh: 寻找最棒的美味。

sentences.en: Who sort of turned cooking instruction shows into these sporting events.
sentences.zh: 他们把烹饪教学节目变成了体育赛事。

sentences.en: And it created a celebrity around restaurants that just did not exist before.
sentences.zh: 这在餐厅周围创造了一种以前不存在的名人效应。

sentences.en: Just exploding the restaurant and the chef culture out into the broader culture, right?
sentences.zh: 把餐厅和厨师文化推向了更广泛的文化领域，对吧？

sentences.en: That suddenly everybody was talking about it.
sentences.zh: 突然间每个人都在谈论它。

sentences.en: Everybody knew about it.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道它。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: And, you know, by the time you get into the early 2000s, you had these celebrity chefs who I think were rightly likened the rock stars.
sentences.zh: 你知道，到了2000年代初，你有了这些被我认为理所当然地比作摇滚明星的名厨。

sentences.en: And the James Beard Awards were right there in the middle of it, becoming more and more relevant because chef culture was becoming more and more relevant.
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯·比尔德奖就处于这一切的中心，随着厨师文化变得越来越重要，它也变得越来越有影响力。

sentences.en: I mean, I have a little bit of reflection of how drastic the change was in my own professional experience.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我对自己职业经历中这种巨大的变化有一点反思。

sentences.en: I started as a restaurant writer and a food writer in the mid-90s in Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: 我90年代中期在华盛顿特区开始担任餐厅评论员和美食作家。

sentences.en: And at the time, I was working for a paper that had never covered food before and that it wasn't a job that people particularly envied.
sentences.zh: 当时，我为一家从未报道过美食的报纸工作，那并不是一份令人羡慕的工作。

sentences.en: And by the end of that time at that job, I left that job in 2000,
sentences.zh: 到我2000年离开那份工作时，

sentences.en: you know, I started going to cocktail parties and people were asking me about my work all of a sudden.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我开始参加鸡尾酒会，人们突然开始问我关于工作的事情。

sentences.en: For reasons that went beyond wanting to know where to get good Vietnamese food.
sentences.zh: 原因不仅仅是想知道去哪里能吃到好的越南菜。

sentences.en: They wanted to know if I'd met these people.
sentences.zh: 他们想知道我是否见过这些人。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有趣。

sentences.en: When I moved to New Orleans in 2000 to take a job at the Daily Newspaper here, Emeril Lagasse had a show that was about to debut, a sitcom.
sentences.zh: 2000年我搬到新奥尔良去当地日报工作时，埃梅里尔·拉加斯有一档即将首播的节目，一部情景喜剧。

sentences.en: Remember Emeril, just be yourself.
sentences.zh: 记住埃梅里尔，做你自己就好。

sentences.en: Okay, so.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那么。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Produced by the same people that created Designing Women on NBC.
sentences.zh: 由NBC《设计女性》的制作团队制作。

sentences.en: And now what we're going to do is add some essence.
sentences.zh: 现在我们要做的就是加点精华。

sentences.en: Bam.
sentences.zh: 砰。

sentences.en: Now, I'm digging myself here, but that was a big deal, right?
sentences.zh: 现在，我是在自嘲，但这可是件大事，对吧？

sentences.en: That was when network television was the biggest platform for a mass market.
sentences.zh: 那是电视网络作为大众市场最大平台的时代。

sentences.en: And he was on the same network as Seinfeld was on.
sentences.zh: 而且他和《宋飞正传》在同一个电视网播出。

sentences.en: So food really had become culture.
sentences.zh: 所以食物真的已经变成了文化。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: And then that culture sort of expanded.
sentences.zh: 然后这种文化开始扩张。

sentences.en: And you have the arrival of, importantly, Anthony Bourdain and his book Kitchen Confidential, which came out in 2000.
sentences.zh: 重要的是，安东尼·波登和他的书《厨房机密》在2000年问世了。

sentences.en: And I think established sort of this punk attitude in celebrity chef culture that was kind of a reaction to the, you know,
sentences.zh: 我认为它在名厨文化中建立了一种朋克态度，这在某种程度上是对……的回应，你知道，

sentences.en: the arena rock bombast of what you saw in the Food Network.
sentences.zh: 你在美食频道看到的那些竞技场摇滚式的浮夸。

sentences.en: Right, small shows and kind of grittier, dirtier, and less polished.
sentences.zh: 没错，小节目，更粗犷、更肮脏、更不加修饰。

sentences.en: Yeah, the restaurant world that Bourdain captured was one that was populated by bandits who didn't play by the rules.
sentences.zh: 是的，波登所描绘的餐饮世界里充满了不按常理出牌的“强盗”。

sentences.en: They worked in environments that, in his view, not everyone could hack.
sentences.zh: 他们工作在那种他认为并非人人都能应付的环境中。

sentences.en: And they didn't go chasing after celebrity.
sentences.zh: 他们不追求名气。

sentences.en: They didn't look presentable for cameras.
sentences.zh: 他们不在镜头前装模作样。

sentences.en: They had knives.
sentences.zh: 他们手里有刀。

sentences.en: They worked around blood.
sentences.zh: 他们在血腥中工作。

sentences.en: They were cutting apart animals, right?
sentences.zh: 他们在切割动物，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, this was a very different look at the restaurant world than we had been accustomed to on the Food Network.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这与我们在美食频道习惯看到的餐饮世界大不相同。

sentences.en: And not for the faint of heart.
sentences.zh: 而且不适合胆小的人。

sentences.en: It wasn't for the faint of heart.
sentences.zh: 它不适合胆小的人。

sentences.en: And I think the movement that Anthony Bourdain helped create, where you have this pirate version of the chef, the James Beard Awards honored all of these.
sentences.zh: 我认为安东尼·波登帮助创造的运动，那种“海盗版”厨师的形象，詹姆斯·比尔德奖都给予了认可。

sentences.en: They honored the celebrity chefs.
sentences.zh: 他们认可了名厨。

sentences.en: They honored the pirate version of the chefs.
sentences.zh: 他们认可了“海盗版”厨师。

sentences.en: They honored restaurants with white tablecloths and without white tablecloths.
sentences.zh: 他们认可了铺着白桌布和没铺白桌布的餐厅。

sentences.en: And through the 2000s and into the 2010s, you saw this expanding audience for this expanded idea of what a chef can be and what a restaurant can deliver.
sentences.zh: 从2000年代到2010年代，你看到了受众对厨师和餐厅所能提供的服务有了更广泛的认知。

sentences.en: And the foundation benefited by being the foremost entity to validate excellence among all these different archetypes.
sentences.zh: 而基金会通过成为验证所有这些不同原型卓越性的首要实体而获益。

sentences.en: So as food becomes a bigger and bigger part of culture and the chefs' profiles rise, the awards themselves become more prominent.
sentences.zh: 所以随着食物在文化中占据越来越重要的地位，厨师的形象提升，奖项本身也变得更加突出。

sentences.en: And suddenly, the awards have become arbiters of culture.
sentences.zh: 突然间，这些奖项成了文化的仲裁者。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And this ecosystem seems to be working for just about all involved until something really big happens.
sentences.zh: 这个生态系统似乎对所有参与者都很有效，直到发生了一件大事。

sentences.en: Now to those new allegations of sexual misconduct rocking the food industry.
sentences.zh: 现在来看那些震撼餐饮界的性骚扰新指控。

sentences.en: Very early on in the Me Too movement, the subjects of some of the most explosive investigations into the behavior of people included people like Mario Batali.
sentences.zh: 在“我也是”运动早期，一些针对个人行为的最具爆炸性的调查对象中，就包括像马里奥·巴塔利这样的人。

sentences.en: The Times reports that in March, a woman told investigators that Batali drugged and sexually assaulted her in January of 2004 at his New York City restaurant.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》报道称，3月份，一名女性告诉调查人员，巴塔利在2004年1月于他纽约市的餐厅里对她下药并进行了性侵犯。

sentences.en: One of the most famous chefs in restaurants in America, a beard winner himself.
sentences.zh: 美国最著名的厨师和餐厅老板之一，他本人也是比尔德奖得主。

sentences.en: Batali gave this statement to the Post saying, I apologize profoundly to the people I have mistreated and hurt.
sentences.zh: 巴塔利向《邮报》发表声明称：“我向那些被我虐待和伤害过的人深表歉意。”

sentences.en: All of a sudden, these people that we were idolizing and celebrating start to be looked at with scrutiny.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，我们曾经崇拜和赞美的人开始受到审视。

sentences.en: And we start asking questions as a culture about how the people who are employees of these restaurants, who don't really benefit from that celebrity, how they're being treated,
sentences.zh: 我们开始作为一个文化群体提出问题：那些餐厅的员工，那些并没有从名气中获益的人，他们是如何被对待的，

sentences.en: and if they're being treated fairly.
sentences.zh: 以及他们是否受到了公平对待。

sentences.en: And what we should think about that industry and that part of our culture based on what we discover.
sentences.zh: 基于我们的发现，我们应该如何看待那个行业和我们文化中的那一部分。

sentences.en: Where I live in New Orleans, a chef named John Besh was the subject of an investigation that I did.
sentences.zh: 在我居住的新奥尔良，一位名叫约翰·贝什的厨师就是我所做调查的对象。

sentences.en: And he was far and away the most famous food figure in a town that is basically defined by its culinary reputation.
sentences.zh: 在一个基本上由烹饪声誉定义的城市里，他无疑是最著名的美食人物。

sentences.en: There was comments about what we were wearing, how we looked in the office, but then also...
sentences.zh: 当时有人议论我们的穿着，议论我们在办公室里的样子，但除此之外……

sentences.en: I found that this prominent restaurant company had what we would now call a toxic culture.
sentences.zh: 我发现这家知名餐饮公司存在我们现在所说的“有毒文化”。

sentences.en: And then he asked me if I would come back to his hotel room with him.
sentences.zh: 然后他问我愿不愿意跟他回酒店房间。

sentences.en: And I told him no, stormed out of the bar.
sentences.zh: 我拒绝了他，并冲出了酒吧。

sentences.en: There were no written words...
sentences.zh: 当时没有任何书面规定……

sentences.en: Women in particular felt that they were sort of second-class citizens and that poor treatment of them was tolerated and maybe even in some instances encouraged.
sentences.zh: 女性尤其感到自己像是二等公民，对她们的恶劣对待不仅被容忍，甚至在某些情况下还受到纵容。

sentences.en: And I told him, you and I both know the reason that we're here goes back to when I wouldn't have sex with John.
sentences.zh: 我告诉他，你我都清楚，我们之所以会走到这一步，是因为我当年拒绝了约翰的性要求。

sentences.en: And that is why I'm being fired right now.
sentences.zh: 而这就是我现在被解雇的原因。

sentences.en: Both the Mario Batali and John Besh stories, I think, really opened the floodgates in the restaurant industry.
sentences.zh: 我认为，马里奥·巴塔利（Mario Batali）和约翰·贝什（John Besh）的事件真正打开了餐饮业的潘多拉魔盒。

sentences.en: And in my own personal experience, in the aftermath of the Besh investigation,
sentences.zh: 就我个人的经历而言，在贝什调查事件之后，

sentences.en: I conducted over 100 interviews in the months after that came out here in New Orleans when I was working at the local newspaper.
sentences.zh: 在那件事曝光后的几个月里，我在当地报社工作期间，在新奥尔良进行了100多次采访。

sentences.en: And that's a lot of people coming forward and saying, I've got a story of abuse that I experienced in a restaurant that I think you need to hear about.
sentences.zh: 很多人站出来说：我经历过餐饮业的虐待，我觉得你需要听听我的故事。

sentences.en: And I remember feeling, I really owe it to these folks to hear them out, that I need to be part of this reckoning in the business.
sentences.zh: 我记得当时的感觉是，我真的有义务倾听这些人的心声，我需要参与到这场行业清算中来。

sentences.en: And I imagine the James Beard Foundation felt something similar.
sentences.zh: 我想詹姆斯·比尔德基金会（James Beard Foundation）可能也有类似的感觉。

sentences.en: That they needed to do something to fix this culture that they had benefited from and maybe even help to foster.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得必须采取行动，来纠正这种他们曾从中受益、甚至可能在某种程度上助长了的文化。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后回来。

sentences.en: Thirty-three presidents.
sentences.zh: 三十三位总统。

sentences.en: I called the president at 4.30 in the morning and he answered.
sentences.zh: 我在凌晨四点半给总统打了电话，他接听了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 太空探索的七十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗恒星之外有什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 一千份消费品指南。

sentences.en: Today I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天我正在测试七款床垫。

sentences.en: Sixty super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 六十款超级圣代。

sentences.en: They were probably the best team in the league every single year.
sentences.zh: 他们可能每年都是联盟中最强的队伍。

sentences.en: Fifty-three thousand five hundred puzzles.
sentences.zh: 五万三千五百个拼图。

sentences.en: I use a different starting word every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天都用不同的起始词。

sentences.en: Twenty-five thousand recipes.
sentences.zh: 两万五千份食谱。

sentences.en: And I love a one-pan recipe because I don't love washing pans.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢“一锅出”的食谱，因为我不喜欢洗锅。

sentences.en: The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: Celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 庆祝175年来我们一直致力于帮助您了解世界，并充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 现在订阅可享特别优惠，请访问 nytimes.com/subscribe。

sentences.en: So Brett, after Me Too, what does the James Beard Foundation decide to do?
sentences.zh: 那么布雷特，在“我也是”（Me Too）运动之后，詹姆斯·比尔德基金会决定怎么做？

sentences.en: Well, as far as we know, they don't do anything substantive to the awards program in the immediate aftermath.
sentences.zh: 据我们所知，在事件发生后的第一时间，他们并没有对奖项评选程序做出任何实质性的改变。

sentences.en: But in 2020, the foundation abruptly canceled the awards, which is something they'd never done before.
sentences.zh: 但在2020年，基金会突然取消了奖项评选，这是他们从未做过的事。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: There's two reasons that we know about.
sentences.zh: 我们所知的有两个原因。

sentences.en: The foundation's leaders discovered that there was no Black winners in the awards that year in any of their major categories.
sentences.zh: 基金会领导层发现，那一年的奖项中，主要类别里竟然没有一位黑人获奖者。

sentences.en: And that happened while there was racial justice protests unfolding all over the country in the aftermath of the George Floyd murder.
sentences.zh: 而这正值乔治·弗洛伊德（George Floyd）遇害后，全国各地爆发种族正义抗议活动期间。

sentences.en: Also, there was accusations that a number of the finalists were guilty of some of the misbehavior that we saw revealed in the Me Too movement.
sentences.zh: 此外，还有指控称，多名入围者涉及我们在“我也是”运动中揭露的一些不当行为。

sentences.en: And so what they did is they ended up canceling not just the 2020 awards, but the 2021 awards.
sentences.zh: 所以他们最终不仅取消了2020年的奖项，还取消了2021年的奖项。

sentences.en: And they used that time to really try to overhaul their awards system.
sentences.zh: 他们利用这段时间试图彻底改革其评奖体系。

sentences.en: And what exactly did they do?
sentences.zh: 他们具体做了什么？

sentences.en: Well, it did three big things.
sentences.zh: 他们做了三件大事。

sentences.en: The first was that it changed its voting body so that now the voting body is made up entirely of judges that are handpicked by the foundation.
sentences.zh: 首先是改变了投票机构，现在的投票成员完全由基金会亲自挑选的评委组成。

sentences.en: So, in other words, more control over the vote.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，就是对投票过程有更多的控制权。

sentences.en: More control.
sentences.zh: 更多的控制权。

sentences.en: And they've created a deliberately a more diverse voting body.
sentences.zh: 而且他们特意建立了一个更加多元化的投票群体。

sentences.en: They also created a code of ethics that they require all candidates for awards follow.
sentences.zh: 他们还制定了一套道德准则，要求所有奖项候选人必须遵守。

sentences.en: So, if you are going to be eligible for a James Beard Award, you vow to the foundation that you follow its code of ethics.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你想获得詹姆斯·比尔德奖的资格，你就必须向基金会承诺遵守其道德准则。

sentences.en: And what was in the code?
sentences.zh: 准则里包含什么内容？

sentences.en: What do they want you to follow?
sentences.zh: 他们要求遵守什么？

sentences.en: Well, the code basically says that, you know, you're not allowed to treat people poorly.
sentences.zh: 准则基本上就是说，你不能恶劣地对待他人。

sentences.en: You're not allowed to treat people unfairly.
sentences.zh: 你不能不公平地对待他人。

sentences.en: And you're not allowed to commit felonies.
sentences.zh: 而且你不能触犯重罪。

sentences.en: And that code of ethics is important.
sentences.zh: 那套道德准则很重要。

sentences.en: And it leads to the third big thing they did,
sentences.zh: 它引出了他们做的第三件大事，

sentences.en: which is the foundation created a tip line so that people can call into the foundation and inform them if they believe any of their candidates have violated this code of ethics.
sentences.zh: 那就是基金会设立了一条举报热线，人们可以致电基金会，告知他们是否认为候选人违反了道德准则。

sentences.en: And then they created a process to investigate those tips.
sentences.zh: 然后他们建立了一套调查这些举报的流程。

sentences.en: So, suddenly, the James Beard Foundation, which started as this kind of tiny dinner club, is turning itself into a de facto investigative body, which is quite different.
sentences.zh: 于是，詹姆斯·比尔德基金会这个最初只是个小型餐饮俱乐部的地方，突然把自己变成了一个事实上的调查机构，这非常不同寻常。

sentences.en: And it's doing that in an industry which, as we all know, post Me Too, is filled with some pretty difficult figures.
sentences.zh: 而且它是在一个行业里做这件事，众所周知，在“我也是”运动之后，这个行业里充斥着一些相当棘手的人物。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And this process is inherently difficult.
sentences.zh: 而且这个过程本身就很困难。

sentences.en: When the Beard Foundation gets these tips through this tip line, they have an ethics committee, which is made up of volunteers, that looks into the allegations.
sentences.zh: 当比尔德基金会通过热线收到举报时，他们有一个由志愿者组成的道德委员会来审查这些指控。

sentences.en: And they determine whether or not they're worth opening an investigation.
sentences.zh: 他们会决定这些指控是否值得展开调查。

sentences.en: And if they do determine that the accusations are worth looking into, they hire outside investigators to do that work.
sentences.zh: 如果他们认为指控值得调查，就会聘请外部调查人员来完成这项工作。

sentences.en: So they're essentially outsourcing an investigation into what is probably some pretty sensitive allegations.
sentences.zh: 所以他们本质上是将针对一些可能非常敏感的指控的调查外包了出去。

sentences.en: They really are.
sentences.zh: 确实是这样。

sentences.en: And in the lead up to the awards this year, this redesigned awards program really came into public view for the first time.
sentences.zh: 在今年颁奖典礼前的筹备阶段，这个重新设计的评奖程序首次进入公众视野。

sentences.en: A chef named Timothy Hansas, who is based in Birmingham, Alabama, was a nominee for Best Chef South, was disqualified.
sentences.zh: 一位常驻阿拉巴马州伯明翰的厨师蒂莫西·汉萨斯（Timothy Hansas），曾是“南方最佳厨师”的提名人，但他被取消了资格。

sentences.en: And he spoke publicly about it to reporters because he felt he was being treated unfairly.
sentences.zh: 他向记者公开谈论了这件事，因为他觉得受到了不公平对待。

sentences.en: He says that he received phone calls from private investigators that were working for the James Beard Foundation and were looking into accusations that he yelled at employees and customers at his restaurant.
sentences.zh: 他说他接到了为詹姆斯·比尔德基金会工作的私家侦探打来的电话，对方正在调查他曾在餐厅对员工和顾客大吼大叫的指控。

sentences.en: So, Brett, you reported this.
sentences.zh: 所以，布雷特，是你报道了这件事。

sentences.en: You looked into it.
sentences.zh: 你对此进行了调查。

sentences.en: What did you find?
sentences.zh: 你发现了什么？

sentences.en: I talked to some people, both customers and past employees, who said that Hansas' behavior was alarming.
sentences.zh: 我采访了一些人，包括顾客和前员工，他们都说汉萨斯的行为令人担忧。

sentences.en: But when I interviewed Hansas, he told me that he doesn't deny any of these accusations.
sentences.zh: 但当我采访汉萨斯时，他告诉我他并不否认这些指控。

sentences.en: He just says everything he's accused of is not as severe as the accusers are telling Beard Foundation,
sentences.zh: 他只是说，他被指控的一切并没有指控者向比尔德基金会描述的那样严重，

sentences.en: and that none of them rise to the level of him having violated the code of ethics.
sentences.zh: 而且这些行为都没有达到违反道德准则的程度。

sentences.en: He said that his problem really was with the process itself.
sentences.zh: 他说他真正的问题在于程序本身。

sentences.en: He believes it wasn't fair.
sentences.zh: 他认为这不公平。

sentences.en: He believes he didn't get due process.
sentences.zh: 他认为自己没有得到正当程序。

sentences.en: He, for example, doesn't know who they talked to.
sentences.zh: 例如，他不知道他们采访了谁。

sentences.en: And, you know, usually in a situation like this, you get to face your accuser, you get to hear what the accusation is, and you get to defend yourself at every step of the way.
sentences.zh: 通常在这种情况下，你有权与指控者对质，有权听取指控内容，并在每一个环节为自己辩护。

sentences.en: But in this case, he only had one conversation with investigators.
sentences.zh: 但在这种情况下，他只与调查人员进行了一次谈话。

sentences.en: Then they went away for a few weeks, and then he gets an email one day saying he's been disqualified.
sentences.zh: 然后他们消失了几周，有一天他突然收到一封邮件，说他被取消了资格。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's like a grand jury proceeding that, you know, happens behind closed doors in secret, except in this case, at the end of it, there's a verdict, and he's guilty.
sentences.zh: 这就像大陪审团的程序，在闭门会议中秘密进行，只不过在这种情况下，最后有一个裁决，而他被判有罪。

sentences.en: Effectively, that's the case.
sentences.zh: 实际上就是这样。

sentences.en: And it turns out that he wasn't even the only candidate that was under investigation by the foundation this year.
sentences.zh: 而且事实证明，他甚至不是今年唯一一个受到基金会调查的候选人。

sentences.en: The other chef's name is Sam Fore, and she works in Lexington, Kentucky, and she was a finalist in the Best Chef Southeast category.
sentences.zh: 另一位厨师叫萨姆·福尔（Sam Fore），她在肯塔基州列克星敦工作，是“东南最佳厨师”类别的决赛入围者。

sentences.en: Sam has a restaurant called Tuk Tuk, and it actually is not even a brick-and-mortar restaurant.
sentences.zh: 萨姆经营着一家名为“Tuk Tuk”的餐厅，它甚至不是一家实体店。

sentences.en: It's a pop-up restaurant that serves sort of Southern cuisine inspired by the Sri Lankan food that she grew up eating in a family of Sri Lankan immigrants in Kentucky.
sentences.zh: 这是一家快闪餐厅，供应受斯里兰卡美食启发的南方菜，那是她在肯塔基州的斯里兰卡移民家庭中从小吃到大的味道。

sentences.en: On the very day that Hanses went public with his own investigation and his issues with it, she received a call from private investigators herself.
sentences.zh: 就在汉萨斯公开他所受的调查及其相关问题的那一天，她自己也接到了私家侦探的电话。

sentences.en: Fore said that the investigators were looking into accusations that were made to the Beard Foundation's tip line
sentences.zh: 福尔说，调查人员正在调查向比尔德基金会举报热线提出的指控，

sentences.en: that she was bullying people and harassing them through her social media posts.
sentences.zh: 称她通过社交媒体帖子欺凌和骚扰他人。

sentences.en: She shared with me examples of a couple of the posts that she was asked about.
sentences.zh: 她与我分享了几个被问及的帖子示例。

sentences.en: One was a public service announcement that she had made as part of a sexual violence awareness campaign that she did in her community.
sentences.zh: 其中一个是她作为社区性暴力意识宣传活动的一部分而发布的公共服务公告。

sentences.en: Others were posts that made accusations about people in her community, but that never named them.
sentences.zh: 其他帖子则是对社区里的人提出指控，但从未指名道姓。

sentences.en: And this was something she said she was mystified by, and she said that she asked the investigators, look, we've been talking now for 90 minutes,
sentences.zh: 她说对此感到非常困惑，她问调查人员：听着，我们已经谈了90分钟了，

sentences.en: and you can't even tell me who I'm targeting with this bullying.
sentences.zh: 你们甚至说不出我这种欺凌行为针对的是谁。

sentences.en: How can this be targeted harassment?
sentences.zh: 这怎么能算是有针对性的骚扰呢？

sentences.en: Oh my gosh, right?
sentences.zh: 天哪，是吧？

sentences.en: And as a reminder, for Fore, the stakes here are really high.
sentences.zh: 提醒一下，对于福尔来说，这里的利害关系非常大。

sentences.en: A nomination could make a huge difference for a chef running a pop-up restaurant.
sentences.zh: 对于经营快闪餐厅的厨师来说，获得提名可能会带来巨大的改变。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, Fore said that after she became a semifinalist for the Beard Awards this year, she hired a public relations firm for the first time in her life.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，福尔说，在今年成为比尔德奖半决赛入围者后，她有生以来第一次聘请了一家公关公司。

sentences.en: And her business, up until quite recently, included only one employee, herself.
sentences.zh: 而她的生意直到最近还只有一名员工，那就是她自己。

sentences.en: So she's in sort of heady territory here.
sentences.zh: 所以她现在处于一个相当令人头晕目眩的境地。

sentences.en: Ultimately, Sam found out that she wasn't disqualified as a result of this investigation.
sentences.zh: 最终，萨姆发现她并没有因为这次调查而被取消资格。

sentences.en: But in the end, she felt like she'd been really put through the ringer for what she says are really bizarre complaints.
sentences.zh: 但最终，她觉得因为一些她所说的“极其荒谬”的投诉，自己被狠狠地折磨了一番。

sentences.en: Brett, what does the James Beard Foundation say about all of this?
sentences.zh: 布雷特，詹姆斯·比尔德基金会对这一切有什么说法？

sentences.en: Like, what's their response?
sentences.zh: 他们的回应是什么？

sentences.en: Well, their blanket response is that they don't comment about any ethics investigations.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们的统一回应是，他们不对任何道德调查发表评论。

sentences.en: They say they do this because they are committed to celebrating the industry and not shaming people,
sentences.zh: 他们说这样做是因为他们致力于赞美这个行业，而不是羞辱他人，

sentences.en: and that they want to protect the identity of both the accusers and the accused.
sentences.zh: 而且他们想保护指控者和被指控者的身份。

sentences.en: I did continue to talk to leaders over there about this commitment to confidentiality,
sentences.zh: 我确实继续与那里的领导层讨论了这种对保密性的承诺，

sentences.en: which I think raises other problems that both Hansas and Fore didn't even bring up themselves.
sentences.zh: 我认为这引发了其他一些问题，甚至连汉萨斯和福尔自己都没有提到。

sentences.en: For instance, Hansas, even though he's publicly known to have been disqualified, his name remained on the ballot until the close of the judging for this year's awards.
sentences.zh: 例如，汉萨斯虽然被公开取消了资格，但他的名字一直留在选票上，直到今年奖项评选结束。

sentences.en: Effectively, that meant that people could vote for Hansas to win an award that he had been disqualified for publicly.
sentences.zh: 实际上，这意味着人们可以投票给一个已经被公开取消资格的汉萨斯，让他获奖。

sentences.en: Crazy.
sentences.zh: 太疯狂了。

sentences.en: Like, that's just a fundamental flaw in the process, right?
sentences.zh: 这简直是程序上的根本性缺陷，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, they didn't think it through.
sentences.zh: 他们根本没考虑周全。

sentences.en: Well, it even goes further, because I asked then, well, will his name appear on the program at the gala in Chicago?
sentences.zh: 嗯，情况甚至更糟，因为我当时问：那么他的名字会出现在芝加哥颁奖典礼的节目单上吗？

sentences.en: And they said yes, that their commitment to confidentiality even extended to that, which then puts the foundation in this position of having discovered that a candidate is actually
sentences.zh: 他们说是的，他们对保密性的承诺甚至延伸到了这一点，这让基金会陷入了一种境地：他们发现一名候选人实际上

sentences.en: not worthy of the award by their own standard, but is remaining a nominee in the eyes of the public.
sentences.zh: 按照他们自己的标准不配获奖，但在公众眼中，他仍然是一名提名人。

sentences.en: I mean, that just doesn't make any sense.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这根本说不通。

sentences.en: That's what I thought.
sentences.zh: 我也是这么想的。

sentences.en: It does seem to be a flaw with this process.
sentences.zh: 这似乎确实是这个程序的一个缺陷。

sentences.en: And when I asked leaders there, they wouldn't come out and say that.
sentences.zh: 当我问那里的领导时，他们不愿明说。

sentences.en: And what I was left to believe is they just never entertained a scenario in which someone would go public with their disqualification.
sentences.zh: 我只能认为，他们从未预料到会有人公开自己的取消资格事件。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有意思。

sentences.en: I mean, maybe, Brett, it just isn't all that surprising that, in some ways, given that this is a food foundation, a tiny one,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，布雷特，也许这并不令人惊讶，考虑到这是一个食品基金会，一个很小的机构，

sentences.en: and it's taken it upon itself to be a kind of version of the FBI, or at the very least, you know, some kind of professional HR department,
sentences.zh: 却承担起了类似联邦调查局的角色，或者至少是某种专业的人力资源部门，

sentences.en: to effectively endeavor what really amounts to a very muscular investigation into personal behavior and potential abuse.
sentences.zh: 去有效地进行一场针对个人行为和潜在虐待的、非常强硬的调查。

sentences.en: Yeah, I do think that they did not anticipate how adversarial such investigations could become.
sentences.zh: 是的，我确实认为他们没有预料到这种调查会变得如此具有对抗性。

sentences.en: I do believe that they thought that the respect for the foundation was such that people in the chef community would just accept the decisions that were being made.
sentences.zh: 我确实相信他们认为，人们对基金会的尊重程度足以让厨师界的人接受所做的决定。

sentences.en: My experience as a reporter, as well as the co-author on this story, Julia Moskin, you know, we both have done a lot of these sorts of investigations.
sentences.zh: 作为一名记者，以及这篇报道的合著者朱莉娅·莫斯金（Julia Moskin），我们都做过很多此类调查。

sentences.en: And even ones that don't lead to stories do end up with some pretty hard feelings on the part of people who are being asked about this behavior.
sentences.zh: 即使是那些没有写成报道的调查，最终也会让那些被问及此类行为的人感到非常不快。

sentences.en: And the foundation is primarily in the business of celebrating this industry.
sentences.zh: 而基金会的主要业务是赞美这个行业。

sentences.en: And, you know, it raises money based on having good relationships with people in the chef industry who cook at fundraisers for the foundation.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，他们通过与厨师行业中那些为基金会筹款活动烹饪的人保持良好关系来筹集资金。

sentences.en: So, Brett, when you look at the issues facing the food industry and the process that the James Beard Foundation put into place to address those issues,
sentences.zh: 所以，布雷特，当你审视食品行业面临的问题以及詹姆斯·比尔德基金会为解决这些问题而制定的程序时，

sentences.en: I guess what I'm really wondering is, is all of this really aimed at reforming chefs?
sentences.zh: 我真正想知道的是，这一切真的是为了改造厨师吗？

sentences.en: I mean, actually forcing change and forcing better behavior?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，真的在强制改变和强制更好的行为吗？

sentences.en: Or is there a simpler and more self-serving explanation, which is, you know, that they're really just after protecting themselves, protecting the James Beard Foundation, you know,
sentences.zh: 还是有一个更简单、更自私的解释，那就是他们实际上只是为了保护自己，保护詹姆斯·比尔德基金会，

sentences.en: saving themselves from being embarrassed by bad publicity?
sentences.zh: 让自己免受负面宣传的尴尬？

sentences.en: To be honest, I think it's both.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我认为两者都有。

sentences.en: I think the second reason is inarguable.
sentences.zh: 我认为第二个原因是不容置疑的。

sentences.en: And I think it applies to all of the institutions that are in the food industry in the aftermath of Me Too.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这适用于“我也是”运动后食品行业的所有机构。

sentences.en: That said, I think it's an open question as to whether or not a program like this, an investigatory program, can have a real effect on a restaurant business
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，我认为像这样的调查项目是否能对餐饮业产生真正的影响，仍然是一个悬而未决的问题，

sentences.en: where bad behavior continues to be a persistent problem.
sentences.zh: 因为不良行为仍然是一个持续存在的问题。

sentences.en: I mean, we know there was a flood of media reports following Me Too and in the years since Me Too about bad behavior in the restaurant industry.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们都知道在“我也是”（Me Too）运动之后，以及随后的几年里，媒体大量报道了餐饮业中的不良行为。

sentences.en: And we know that that didn't eliminate bad behavior from the restaurant industry.
sentences.zh: 我们也知道，这些报道并没有消除餐饮业中的不良行为。

sentences.en: It did not have that effect, right?
sentences.zh: 它并没有产生那种效果，对吧？

sentences.en: I think it probably reduced the number of people who feel like they are entitled to abuse their power, but it certainly didn't eradicate power abuse from the restaurant business.
sentences.zh: 我想它可能减少了那些自认为有权滥用职权的人数，但它肯定没有根除餐饮业中的权力滥用。

sentences.en: And to be honest, I'm not sure what will.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我不确定什么才能做到这一点。

sentences.en: But Brett, isn't there also a scenario where this process, as clumsy as it is, might accidentally lead to something good?
sentences.zh: 但是布雷特，难道不存在这样一种情况吗：这个过程虽然笨拙，却可能意外地带来一些好的结果？

sentences.en: I think that it could.
sentences.zh: 我认为是有可能的。

sentences.en: And, you know, the process could improve.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这个过程是可以改进的。

sentences.en: I find it hard to believe, though, that you could have an award that routinely disqualifies people that won't routinely find itself in the midst of controversy.
sentences.zh: 不过，我很难相信，一个经常取消获奖者资格的奖项，能够避免陷入争议之中。

sentences.en: Brett, thank you.
sentences.zh: 布雷特，谢谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: It's a pleasure to be on the show.
sentences.zh: 很高兴能参加这个节目。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Winnalou.
sentences.zh: 我是温娜露。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我负责编写《纽约时报》游戏中的谜题之一——《连接》（Connections）。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我热爱恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我也喜欢尝试捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖斯基，我每天负责制作《拼字蜜蜂》（Spelling Bee）和《字母盒子》（Letterboxd）游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做“联觉”（promesthesia）的特质。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我在听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由像你们刚才听到的这些人制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 请访问 nytimes.com/games 开始今天的游戏吧。

sentences.en: Here's what else you should know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: Silvio Berlusconi, the Italian media mogul who became Italy's most polarizing and prosecuted prime minister, died on Monday.
sentences.zh: 意大利媒体大亨、曾任意大利最具争议且官司缠身的总理西尔维奥·贝卢斯科尼于周一去世。

sentences.en: He was 86.
sentences.zh: 他享年86岁。

sentences.en: Berlusconi transformed Italian television, making it spectacular and tawdry, and then, as a politician, used it to influence voters.
sentences.zh: 贝卢斯科尼改变了意大利电视业，使其变得既壮观又俗艳，随后，他作为一名政治家，利用电视来影响选民。

sentences.en: Through multiple stints in office,
sentences.zh: 在多次任职期间，

sentences.en: Berlusconi revolutionized Italian politics, bringing a brash populism and perfecting the practice of victimization.
sentences.zh: 贝卢斯科尼彻底改变了意大利政治，带来了粗鲁的民粹主义，并完善了受害者心态的运用。

sentences.en: He was a committed ally of America, but also an apologist for Vladimir Putin.
sentences.zh: 他是美国的坚定盟友，但同时也是弗拉基米尔·普京的辩护者。

sentences.en: In the end, even Berlusconi's many critics agree that he changed Italy, leaving his stamp on a generation of Italians who hungered for the wealth and confidence that he stood for.
sentences.zh: 最终，即使是贝卢斯科尼的许多批评者也承认，他改变了意大利，在他所代表的财富和自信所渴望的一代意大利人身上留下了他的印记。

sentences.en: And,
sentences.zh: 此外，

sentences.en: JPMorgan Chase reached a tentative settlement with sexual abuse victims of Jeffrey Epstein, the financier who died in a New York jail before his trial.
sentences.zh: 摩根大通与杰弗里·爱泼斯坦的性虐待受害者达成了初步和解协议，爱泼斯坦是一位在审判前死于纽约监狱的金融家。

sentences.en: The settlement followed a series of embarrassing disclosures about the bank's longstanding relationship with Epstein.
sentences.zh: 此前，关于该银行与爱泼斯坦长期关系的系列尴尬披露引发了此次和解。

sentences.en: One of the lead lawyers for the victims said the bank was prepared to pay $290 million to resolve the lawsuit, which was filed in Manhattan last November.
sentences.zh: 受害者的一位首席律师表示，该银行准备支付2.9亿美元以解决去年11月在曼哈顿提起的诉讼。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由

sentences.en: Sidney Harper,
sentences.zh: 西德尼·哈珀、

sentences.en: Carlos Prieto, and Ricky Navecki.
sentences.zh: 卡洛斯·普列托和里奇·纳维基制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Devin Taylor and Michael Benoit, contains original music by Marianne Lozano and Dan Powell, and was engineered by Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 节目由德文·泰勒和迈克尔·贝努瓦剪辑，包含玛丽安·洛萨诺和丹·鲍威尔的原创音乐，并由克里斯·伍德进行工程处理。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Landsberg of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由Wonderly的吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰兹伯格创作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Sabrina Tavernisi.
sentences.zh: 我是萨布丽娜·塔弗尼西。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》中，我们将为假期接待客人做准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让客人宾至如归的秘诀。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是需要全黑环境才能入睡的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是否会因为喝醉而睡着。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们需要什么样的光线？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢喝咖啡还是茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on the New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 在《纽约时报》应用程序或你喜欢的任何地方收听《Wirecutter秀》。
